uncited: It builds on [Uniform Ray Marching](4810-uniform-ray-marching.md) by replacing fixed uniform intervals with adaptive step sizes and skipping empty regions via multiscale occupancy grids.
**Inputs:** Ray origin $o$, ray direction $d$, scene bounding box size $s$ (largest axis), NeRF model $f_{\theta}$, current training step $N_{step}$.
**Outputs:** Sample positions along the ray, transmittance, accumulated color.
Cells are laid out in Morton (z-curve) order.
Each cell stores occupancy as a single bit.
**Density Grids:** A second set of $K$ grids with the same layout, storing full-precision floating-point density values.
*   Otherwise, set $\Delta t = t/256$, where $t$ is the current distance along the ray.
*   For a sample position $x$, determine which grid to query.
*   Query the occupancy bit of the cell containing $x$ in the selected grid.
*   Calculate next sample position $x = o + t \cdot d$.
If occupied, query NeRF model $f_{\theta}(x)$ to get density $\sigma$ and color $C$.
*   Accumulate color: $C_{out} \leftarrow C_{out} + T \cdot (1 - \exp(-\sigma \cdot \Delta t)) \cdot C$.
Used in Instant-NGP for fast NeRF training and rendering.
